title: Anand Rathi Wealth Ltd - 543415 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Wealth manager reports H1 FY27 PAT up about 23% to INR 238 crore and record net flows of INR 4,186 crore, but has no capacity or pricing supply signals; AUM guidance trimmed to a 2-3% mark-to-market dependent outlook.

summary.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth H1 FY27 PAT rose ~23% YoY to INR 238 crore (ex non-business items) on record INR 4,186 crore net mobilisation.

financial_highlights.metric: H1 FY27 PAT (ex non-business items: fair value gains, ESOP expenses, related tax)
Q2 FY27 non-cash charges (ESOP and mark-to-market)
financial_highlights.value: INR 46 crore (Rajesh Bhutara; Feroze Azeez first cited ~INR 40 crore)
financial_highlights.change: vs zero in the corresponding quarter last year

financial_highlights.metric: Q2 FY27 equity mutual fund net flow

segments.name: Private wealth (flagship)
segments.commentary: Added 1,500 net new client families in the last 12 months, taking total to 14,309. Team of 431 RMs with capacity for about 8,000 more clients, per management.

segments.name: Digital wealth (B2B2C)
segments.commentary: AUM grew 14% YoY to INR 2,531 crore; client count rose 15% YoY to 7,584.

segments.name: OFA (Omni Financial Advisor, SaaS)
segments.commentary: About 6,898 subscribers with platform assets of about INR 1.66 crore (as stated) at end-September 2026; management noted these are platform assets only.

qa_highlights.question: Wallet share of top 100 clients and how it is measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said platinum clients (over 1.5% of clients) keep 50-60% of their wallet with ARWL, and top 100 clients 60-70%; wealth defined as all assets, not just mutual funds.

qa_highlights.question: Will ESOP costs decline next year and employee cost growth slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Feroze Azeez said non-cash ESOP/MTM costs will reduce dramatically, narrowing the gap between PBT (INR 122 crore) and ~INR 90 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Non-cash charges in the quarter and year-ago comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Rajesh Bhutara said INR 46 crore in Q2 FY27 versus zero in the same quarter last year.

qa_highlights.question: GIFT City revenue opportunity and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will bring NRI and global capital into India via GIFT City, with no revenue provisioned in FY27 guidance until proof of concept; inward-only focus both short and long term.

qa_highlights.question: Net flow split between existing and new clients and strategic priorities?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 split was 62% existing and 38% new; four growth engines cited: client performance, capacity utilisation (431 RMs, room for 8,000 clients), capacity creation (500 account managers), and wallet penetration.

qa_highlights.question: AUM target and sensitivity to markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Target INR 1.2 lakh crore AUM for the year; Q2 AUM about INR 1.08 lakh crore (+18% YoY); mark-to-market hit about INR 2,000 crore in the quarter; management said AUM is the most volatile guidance metric.

qa_highlights.question: SEBI plan to allow PMS to offer mutual fund advisory: competitive threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Feroze Azeez said it is not competitive for ARWL and that RIAs may find a PMS-based mutual fund platform useful.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,415 crore; H1 delivered 49% of it.
FY27 PAT guidance of INR 460 crore; H1 delivered 52% of it, leaving 48% to go.

FY27 AUM target of INR 1.2 lakh crore; net flow target of INR 6,000-8,000 crore for the residual year, per Feroze Azeez's answer to Arun Gopal (later framed as INR 3,000-4,000 crore per quarter for the next two quarters).
Management said it has not provisioned any GIFT City revenue in FY27 guidance.
Management expects ESOP cost to fall 'dramatically' next year; PBT-to-non-cash gap to narrow from INR 122 crore PBT vs ~INR 90 crore cited.
Trail commission target of 50% cited as a stated guidance item, timing not specified.
Mutual fund licence application expected to be filed by end-October 2026.
capex_capacity: GIFT City (IFSCA) approval received; management plans two funds, with launch expected in the next 2-3 months (targeted for the December quarter update).
London, UK operations started in the last quarter.
Mutual fund licence application to be filed by month-end (October 2026), per CFO Rajesh Bhutara.
Technology: management plans to keep spending on technology and hired four IITians for algo research; reinvestment of PBT above ~40% margin into verticals.
Next 100 RMs identified and being trained for promotion over 1-1.5 years; 500 account managers in the pipeline.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 net mobilisation split: 62% from existing clients, 38% from new clients (per Feroze Azeez, consistent with 60-70% existing-client share).
Management says it charges no fee discounts for larger UHNI clients; fee rates are the same or marginally better at higher tiers.
Q2 primary MLD issuance about INR 2,073 crore and secondary about INR 750 crore (per Vishal Sanghavi).
Client acquisition mainly via referrals (50-70% of clientele) and 165 client events in FY26; website leads rising; cold calling to be phased out over 3-4 years.
Feroze Azeez said 1,190 consecutive MLD products met expected returns from Dec 2020 to May-June 2026; some recent products delivered 6-7% vs targeted 14-15%.
risks_watch: Market-linked AUM and mark-to-market volatility; management flagged AUM as the most volatile guidance metric.
Net flow shortfall versus target: lump-sum flows were low and SIPs robust in H1; net flow guidance implies INR 3,000-4,000 crore per quarter.
MLD product returns: some recent products delivered 6-7% against 14-15% targets; management says none have lost money at maturity.
Regulatory approvals pending: mutual fund licence filing and GIFT City launch timing.
Rising non-cash ESOP charges (INR 46 crore in Q2) against nil a year earlier; trail commission target of 50% not yet achieved.
Lack of capacity to take on new RMs quickly; hiring pace controlled to avoid 'biting more than chewing'.
key_quotes: Excluding the impact of non -business-related items, fair value gains, and ESOP exp enses, and related tax effects , Profit After tax, for the first half year of FY27, the PAT grew by -- sorry, after-tax PAT grew by about 23% year-on-year to INR 238 crores, while revenue increased 17% year-on-year to INR 693 crores.

So, near-term, am I worried about the summation of 20%-25% PAT growth? The answer is no. If that was the case with the slightest of the probabilities, I would have revised my PAT guidance down from 460.
So, we say we don't do in low cost. If I don't deserve 1%, I don't want to be on that table.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on client acquisition, flows and long-term strategy, with candid admissions on recent MLD underperformance and a lower-than-expected AUM quarter. Management is often discursive and deflects specifics to colleagues, and gave few hard numbers on GIFT City and MF licence economics.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,415 crore held with 49% achieved in H1 (~17% H1 growth), backed by RM capacity for ~8,000 more clients and record net mobilisation of INR 4,186 crore (+39%); net flow guidance is only partly backed, as it was cut to INR 3,000-4,000 crore per quarter, and GIFT City revenue is excluded from guidance.
